# TableCellOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for [`TableCell`](table-cell.md). Intersects [`BorderedElementOptions`](bordered-element-options.md).

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
type TableCellOptions = BorderedElementOptions & Partial<Omit<Pick<TableCell, TableCellOwnKey>, 'color' | 'padding' | 'verticalAlignment'>> & {
    /** Vertical placement of the content within the row. */
    verticalAlignment?: VerticalAlignmentInput;
    /** Cell text colour. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    color?: ColorInput;
    /** Cell padding. Accepts `12`, `[h, v]`, `[l, t, r, b]` or `{ bottom: 12 }`. */
    padding?: ThicknessInput;
}
```

- [`backgroundColor`](#backgroundcolor): Background fill.
- [`border`](#border): Border widths, and optionally their colour.

- [`content`](#content): The content element to display in this cell

- [`keepWithNext`](#keepwithnext): Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.

### `backgroundColor`

```typescript
backgroundColor?: ColorInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Background fill. Accepts a palette token (`'slate-100'`) or hex.

### `border`

```typescript
border?: BorderInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Border widths, and optionally their colour.

Accepts a uniform width, a per-side object, or `{ width, color }`. Omitted sides are zero.

BonniePDF models widths and colours as separate properties (`border` + `borderColors`), so the colour-carrying form resolves to both. The `border` **property setter** deliberately never writes `borderColors` - a setter must not mutate a sibling - which is why this sugar lives here, in the options layer, and is applied by `applyBorderedElementOptions`.

### `borderColors`

```typescript
borderColors?: BorderColors | undefined
```

*optional*

Border colors for each side of the element

### `breakAllowed`

```typescript
breakAllowed?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this element can be split across page boundaries. When false, the element is treated as atomic and will be moved to a new page rather than split. If it doesn't fit on a fresh page either, it renders anyway. Default is true.

### `captureName`

```typescript
captureName?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot. Unset by default; a future capture API can populate it.

Cell text colour. Accepts a palette token or hex.

### `cornerRadius`

```typescript
cornerRadius?: LengthInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Corner radius. Accepts a length: `6`, `'2mm'`, or `{ value, unit }`.

### `isHeader`

```typescript
isHeader?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this cell is a header cell (renders as `/TH` in PDF/UA tagged output instead of `/TD`). Set automatically by `Table.addHeader*` on each cell in a header row, and at render time from the owning row's `isHeader` flag for cells added directly to a row. Can also be set explicitly for individual cells acting as headers (e.g. first-column row labels).

```typescript

```

Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.
